harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT egress router for node2/node3 (RHEL10), implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the cluster's Ansible control node). node1's eth1 (aliased enp8s0) got a static private-subnet address (10.50.50.254/24) plus a source-NAT masquerade rule on eth0 for 10.50.50.0/24. node2/node3 got static addresses (10.50.50.11/.12) on their second NIC with node1 as gateway (lower-priority default route, metric 200, alongside their existing primary-network route), plus rp_filter=0 on that NIC to stop the kernel dropping NAT-returned replies that arrive asymmetrically relative to the primary route. Verified end-to-end egress (ping + HTTPS) from both private clients through node1's NAT. All four managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot_id captured before/after each restart and full functional/config recovery confirmed afterward (NAT rule, static IPs, rp_filter setting, and live internet reachability through NAT all persisted across node1's reboot).
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes' OS, NICs, and existing routes/config: node1=VyOS 2026-rolling router, node2/node3=RHEL 10 dual-NIC clients on a private enp8s0 segment, node4=Ubuntu 24.04 with ansible-core preinstalled (the designated control node)
Wired passwordless SSH cluster-wide using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY: node4 -> vyos@node1, root@node2, root@node3
Installed vyos.vyos, ansible.netcommon, community.general, ansible.posix Ansible collections on node4

Diagnosed that vyos.vyos_config (network_cli) fails with a generic 'Set failed' against this VyOS build's interactive CLI, and that the classic vyatta-cfg script-template config session silently fails to establish over SSH unless run with become/root (FUSE session setup for the vyos user over non-privileged SSH doesn't create the config mount)

Authored /root/nat-egress/{inventory.ini,ansible.cfg,site.yml,templates/vyos_nat_egress.sh.j2} on node4: play 1 templates+runs a classic-CLI VyOS script (become: yes) to set eth1's address and a NAT source masquerade rule for 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0, then commits/saves; play 2 uses community.general.nmcli to give node2/node3 static private IPs with node1 as gateway (metric 200) and ansible.posix.sysctl to disable rp_filter on their private NIC

Ran the playbook (idempotent on repeat runs) and verified via tcpdump/conntrack on node1 that NAT and forwarding worked but replies were being dropped by node2/node3's own rp_filter due to asymmetric dual-homed routing; fixed via the sysctl task and re-verified successful ping/HTTPS egress from both clients through node1

Captured a boot_id + health baseline on all 4 nodes, then restarted node2, node3, node4, and node1 one at a time (never concurrently), polling exec availability and confirming a changed boot_id after each, and re-verifying NAT rule/static IP/rp_filter/live internet reachability (and Ansible control from node4) after each recovery

evidence.requirement: node1 configured to provide NAT for node2/node3 egress, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook site.yml run from node4 successfully applied VyOS interface/NAT config to node1 and static IP/rp_filter config to node2/node3 (play recap: ok/changed with no failures)

evidence.requirement: NAT egress functionally verified end-to-end from node2 and node3 through node1
evidence.summary: nft masquerade rule hit counters, tcpdump on node1 eth0/eth1, and conntrack confirmed NAT+forwarding worked; root cause of initial failure (rp_filter dropping asymmetric replies on node2/node3) diagnosed and fixed; final curl/ping tests from node2 and node3 via enp8s0 succeeded (ICMP 0% loss, HTTPS 301)

evidence.requirement: node1 boot-identity baseline, restart, changed identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 9028a473... before restart, reboot acknowledged, boot_id 93140578... after restart (changed), NAT rule/eth1 address/ip_forward and live node2+node3 egress through node1 all confirmed healthy post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 boot-identity baseline, restart, changed identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 636556ce... before, 21403f2e... after (changed); static IP, rp_filter=0, and successful ping/HTTPS through node1's NAT confirmed post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 boot-identity baseline, restart, changed identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 7ef78016... before, 2a4cc619... after (changed); static IP, rp_filter=0, and successful ping/HTTPS through node1's NAT confirmed post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 (Ansible control node) boot-identity baseline, restart, changed identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id a6937a34... before, cde01917... after (changed); ansible-core intact and ansible ping against all 3 other nodes succeeded post-restart, confirming control-node functionality recovered
